items.title: Fei-Fei Li’s $8B World Model
items.creator: Welch Labs
items.description: A visual explainer on Fei-Fei Li and world models, starting from the ImageNet years.
items.why_recommended: Welch Labs explains with care, and world models are one of your interests.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A clearer picture of the path from ImageNet to today's world model work.

items.title: Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
items.creator: Lilian Weng
items.description: A survey of how agents and language models score well without doing the intended task.
items.why_recommended: It was published two years ago today and maps the problem well. Newer work will not be in it.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: You will be able to tell a badly specified goal from reward tampering, and name ways RLHF can be gamed.

items.title: Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence?
items.creator: The Quanta Podcast
items.description: Where the attention mechanism came from, and whether predicting words says anything about intelligence.
items.why_recommended: A short, fresh episode that goes past how attention works to what it may be missing.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: You will know why attention was invented for translation, and one case for why it may not be enough on efficiency.

cross_domain.connection: It sets the transformer beside the human brain, which needs far less data and energy.

items.title: Where Is the Friend's House? (1987)
items.creator: Abbas Kiarostami
items.description: A boy takes his classmate's notebook by mistake and sets out to find his home.
items.why_recommended: A quiet, much admired film for a Saturday, built from a very small problem.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: The feeling of how much is at stake in a small duty, seen from a child's height.

items.title: Plan a night for the Geminid meteors (13-14 December)
items.creator: EarthSky
items.description: The Geminids peak on the night of 13-14 December 2026, with little moonlight in the way.
items.why_recommended: About two weeks of notice, if a dark sky is easy to reach. Skip it freely if not.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: The sight of meteors with your own eyes. Find a dark spot, lie back and give it an hour.

items.title: “Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage in End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research” by keshavs, Vivek Hebbar, Julian Stastny, sebastian_prasanna, egan
items.creator: LessWrong (30+ Karma)
items.description: A narrated post on a test of whether auditors can spot secret sabotage in safety research.
items.why_recommended: Nine minutes on a hard question for anyone who lets agents run experiments.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A sense of why a full research log may still not be enough to catch deliberate sabotage.

items.title: We Mapped the Invisible Universe. Something Doesn’t Add Up.
items.creator: PBS Space Time
items.description: How 3D maps of dark matter are being made, and a puzzle they raise.
items.why_recommended: New this week, with a strong like rate for the channel.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: An idea of how something invisible can be mapped, and where the results are still puzzling.

items.title: Politics and the English Language
items.creator: George Orwell
items.description: Orwell's 1946 essay on how vague language and vague thinking feed each other.
items.why_recommended: A classic that helps with explaining research as much as with politics.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Six plain rules you can test on one paragraph of your own writing.

items.title: The Red and The Grey Matter: New Architecture in Africa
items.creator: DW History
items.description: A documentary on new African architecture, including Francis Kéré's Goethe-Institut in Dakar.
items.why_recommended: Something outside the usual: buildings shaped by local materials and traditions.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: You will see why an architect might choose red clay, and how local building methods shape a modern design.

items.title: Music for Nine Post Cards (1982)
items.creator: Hiroshi Yoshimura
items.description: Home-recorded ambient music that Yoshimura imagined playing inside a Tokyo art museum.
items.why_recommended: Gentle listening that suits reading, walking or doing nothing.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A calm half hour, and a sense of how music can be made for a particular space.

items.title: 100 Objects #25: Beaded Moccasin
items.creator: 99% Invisible
items.description: A poet traces the story of a pair of beaded moccasins that hung on a family wall.
items.why_recommended: A personal way into history through one object.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A look at what a family keepsake can reveal about Native boarding schools and the people behind a gift.

items.title: Responding to objections to recursive self-improvement
items.creator: Dwarkesh Podcast
items.description: Dwarkesh Patel answers the strongest objections to his essay on AI improving AI.
items.why_recommended: Useful if you want to test the argument rather than just hear it.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: The main objections, such as whether AI research can be checked, and how well the replies hold.

notes: Podcasts and videos come from the candidate files fetched on 2026-11-27, the latest available.
